text:
marta: Quick follow-up from the design sync this morning. We're moving forward with separating policy evaluation from the console query edge into an orchestrator service. Need to nail the operational playbook before we touch prod.

devon: +1. primary constraints: keep interactive dashboard p99 <= 150ms, no more than 2000 extra decisions/sec cost delta, and revocation TTL for sensitive writes <= 5s.

sam: noted. can we define failure modes up-front? e.g., orchestrator OOM, stream lag, edge cache divergence. each needs a clear rollback and mitigation.

marta: agreed. propose we define three degradation modes and actions:
- mode A: orchestrator slow (p99 up) -> flip affected tenants to edge-only via FF and scale down orchestrator routing
- mode B: invalidation stream lag -> enable direct push for priority keys and increase cache_ttl for non-sensitive reads
- mode C: data drift (policy mismatch) -> run immediate enforced diff and quarantined rollback of the new policy set

akshay: on push vs stream: implement a best-effort push over our mesh for critical revoke events, signed with our service identity. stream remains canonical for full state + replays.

sam: what about atomicity? if an edge applies an outdated decision while orchestrator already denied, users might see confusing errors. suggestion: add a short-lived denial grace window (2s) where edges check with orchestrator for high-value write ops.

devon: that may blow latency. Instead, consider an optimistic read path (edge serves reads), but force coordinator check for any write or permission escalation. write ops are rarer.

marta: agreed with devon: reads stay fast. writes go through orchestrator always in orchestrator-mode. hybrid-mode keeps edge-motion for hot read prefixes.

sam: rollout plan draft:
1) Dry-run: feature flag, no traffic. smoke pipeline: policy parity checker run, unit tests + e2e with canned policies.
2) Canary-1: 1% tenant routing to orchestrator for read-only routes, instrument heavy tracing.
3) Canary-2: 5% with hybrid for reads + orchestrator for writes. enable invalidation stream but don't force-expire yet.
4) Priority revokes: enable push lane for a small set of priority policy keys and run canary revocation tests.
5) Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with staged migration of write routes and enterprise opt-outs.

akshay: make sure we have automated canary tests that flip a policy rule and assert signal within 5s. instrument both stream and push paths.

marta: monitoring TODOs:
- split decision latency (edge-shortcircuit vs orchestrator) p50/p95/p99
- invalidation delivery latency histogram (stream vs push)
- per-tenant decision cost (tokens/CPU/ms)
- rate of mismatch errors (edge vs orchestrator denies)
- audit log sampling keys (1% full context, 0.1% full traces)

devon: logging needs scrubber for PII; sample size targets: 1% decisions for textual context removed, 0.1% with full context for debugging. secure logs must land in compliance bucket with TTL.

sam: ops runbook snippets (short):
- symptom: p99 latency > baseline by 2x -> action: enable edge-only FF for affected prefix, scale orchestrator, open incident page
- symptom: invalidation tail > 5s for priority keys -> action: enable push lane, replay stream from last ack, escalate to infra if kafka consumer lag high
- symptom: mismatch rate spikes (deny vs allow) -> action: pause policy deploys, run diff tool, rollback recent policies, notify security and product

akshay: capacity planning: orchestrator should be horizontally autoscaled with a warm pool to keep cold-start < 10ms. recommend target CPU util 40-60% at normal QPS. add per-tenant burst limiter to protect shared pool.

marta: perf-testing plan: synthetic replay of 5M historical queries across tenants; vary session lengths; run two experiments: orchestrator-only and hybrid. capture p99 CPU network and heap histograms.

devon: cost model: estimate additional egress + compute per million decisions. we need a weekly cost alert during ramp if delta > budget.

sam: security: orchestrator must sign invalidation pushes and stream messages. mutual TLS + rotation. add attestation for the push path.

marta: compatibility: maintain an "edge-decision shim" that can run policy predicates locally for a strict subset (fast predicates only) so we don't have to ship full interpreter to every edge. this reduces coupling and makes rollbacks simpler.

akshay: migration notes for enterprise customers: ship a two-week opt-in period where customers can test orchestrator routing in staging. Clear opt-out API so they stay on edge-only until final cutoff.

ops-bot: test-cluster created: policy-orch-canary-1778889999 (id: pc-1778889999) — scheduled canary window 2026-04-02T02:00Z to 2026-04-02T06:00Z

marta: next actions: I'll write a concise cutover doc (playbook + metrics to watch + rollback criteria) and attach to the RFC. volunteers to review?
devon: i'll take the perf section. sam: i'll own runbooks and canary tests. akshay: i'll handle infra push+auth.

marta: thanks. will ping reviewers in the RFC thread when ready.
